title: Westinghouse to fabricate LEU+ fuel at expanded S.C. facility
summary: Westinghouse has announced that it will invest $1 billion to construct a new plant to fabricate fuel with uranium enriched up to 8 percent U-235 on the site of its Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility (CFFF) in Hopkins, S.C. Westinghouse has completed pre-construction preparation work on the site and, since 2024, has engaged with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission ahead of submitting an application to amend its existing facility license. It aims to produce 600 metric tons uranium of fuel each year beginning in 2030.

title: Nano Nuclear Signs Engineering Agreement With Argentina’s IMPSA For Kronos Microreactor
summary: US advanced reactor developer Nano Nuclear Energy has signed a three-year engineering services agreement with the US subsidiary of Argentina’s IMPSA to assess the design and manufacture of key components for its Kronos microreactor, a statement said. According to the statement, the initial work would be an approximately six-month design review and manufacturing feasibility study, with the reactor pressure vessel a principal component under assessment.

title: NRC finalizes rule on licensing reactors with prior DOE or DOD authorization
summary: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has finalized a rule that would allow applicants with reactor designs already authorized by the Department of Energy or Department of Defense to pursue a streamlined pathway through the NRC’s commercial licensing process.

title: Six AP1000 reactors eyed for Kentucky nuclear power facility
summary: In the latest example of Westinghouse's AP1000 being proposed for new nuclear power capacity, project development firm The Nuclear Company has announced plans to deploy up to six AP1000s along the Ohio River in eastern Kentucky. Dubbed Prosperity One, the proposed power plant site would generate approximately 6.6 GW of new nuclear power if six reactors are ultimately deployed. Not only would it become Kentucky's first nuclear power plant, but it could also become the largest nuclear power generation site in the United States, the company said on Wednesday.

title: Finland Grants Operating Licence To World’s First Deep Geologic Nuclear Repository
summary: Finland has granted an operating licence to Posiva for its spent nuclear fuel encapsulation and final disposal facility at Olkiluoto, marking the first time a deep geological repository for spent nuclear fuel has received an operating licence anywhere in the world. Posiva said the licence allows it to move towards the operational phase of the facility, but does not authorise the immediate start of disposal activities.

title: Entergy New Orleans raises record $175,000 at annual Power to Care Golf Tournament
summary: Entergy New Orleans brought together business and community partners for a day of golf and giving at its annual Power to Care Golf Tournament. The event raised a record $175,000 to help seniors and customers with disabilities facing financial hardship. Source

title: Westinghouse To Invest $1 Billion In New US Higher Enrichment Nuclear Fuel Facility
summary: Westinghouse Electric Company has announced an investment of approximately $1bn (€890m) in a new manufacturing facility for low-enriched uranium plus (LEU+) nuclear fuel at its existing Columbia fuel fabrication site in South Carolina, a statement said. The company said construction has begun at the site near Hopkins. Production is scheduled to start in 2030.
